\chapter{Review --- Four Small Things}
\label{ch:repaso-tonicos}
\hlchaptermodality{250}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can use the stressed pronouns, exclaim, and address somebody.}

I can use the stressed pronouns, exclaim, and address somebody.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[(review)]{(review)}

\label{lesson:ES-C64-repaso-tonicos}



\begin{quote}
After a preposition: \emph{para} \emph{\textbf{mí}}, \emph{para} \emph{\textbf{ti}}, \emph{para} \emph{\textbf{él}}.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Four chants.

\textbf{First.} \emph{El café es para mí.} — the stressed pronouns, and only the first two persons change shape at all.

\textbf{Second.} \emph{¿Vienes conmigo?} — the two that fuse, each carrying \emph{with} at both ends.

\textbf{Third.} \emph{¡Qué bien!} — the asking word exclaiming, accent intact.

\textbf{Fourth.} \emph{María, ven.} — a comma, and that is the whole grammar of addressing somebody.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: the accent has never been about questions}]
Two accents in this chapter, doing two different jobs, and neither is about questions.

On \emph{\textbf{mí}} it separates twins: \emph{mi} is \emph{my}, \emph{mí} is \emph{me}. On \emph{\textbf{qué}} it marks the word carrying the force, which is why it survives into an exclamation and into a reported question that has no marks at all.

And three of this chapter's four rules exist for one reason: Latin's endings fell away, and something audible had to take over. A stressed pronoun, a preposition doubled at both ends, and a comma.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} the four chants, in order
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which \emph{mí} takes the accent? (The one meaning \textbf{me}.)

And what do three of this chapter's four rules have in common? (Latin's \textbf{endings fell away}, and something audible replaced them.)
\end{tcolorbox}
